scenario: A retailer's web app has unpredictable traffic spikes and the team wants to avoid managing servers. Which compute option fits best?

options.text: A fixed fleet of large Compute Engine VMs sized for peak

explanation: Cloud Run is serverless and autoscales (including to zero), so unpredictable spikes need no capacity planning or server management. A fixed fleet sized for peak wastes money, and sole-tenant or bare-metal options add management.

refs.title: Deploy container images to Cloud Run services

scenario: A company must run a legacy app that needs a specific kernel module and full OS control. Which compute option fits?
explanation: A legacy app needing a specific kernel module and full OS control requires IaaS, so Compute Engine VMs fit. Cloud Run, Cloud Run functions and App Engine standard restrict the OS and runtime.

refs.title: gcloud compute instances create | Google Cloud SDK

scenario: A global e-commerce platform needs a relational database with strong consistency across continents. What should be chosen?

options.text: Cloud SQL with cross-region read replicas
options.note: Writes go to one region; replicas lag.
NoSQL, no SQL transactions across rows.

explanation: Spanner in a multi-region configuration gives a relational database with strong (external) consistency across continents and up to 99.999% availability. Cloud SQL read replicas are eventually consistent, and Bigtable and Firestore are NoSQL.

scenario: An IoT platform ingests millions of time-series writes per second and needs single-digit millisecond reads by key. Which database fits?

options.note: In-memory cache without durable storage at this scale.

explanation: Bigtable handles millions of time-series writes per second with single-digit millisecond reads by key. Design row keys to avoid hotspots, for example by not leading with a timestamp. Cloud SQL and BigQuery don't fit that write rate and latency.

scenario: Which database best fits a PostgreSQL app needing high transactional performance plus fast analytical queries on the same data?
explanation: AlloyDB for PostgreSQL combines high transactional performance with a columnar engine for fast analytics on the same data. Firestore and Bigtable aren't PostgreSQL-compatible.

scenario: A team wants a disaster recovery design with an RTO of minutes and RPO near zero for a Cloud SQL database. What's best?

options.text: Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus with cross-region replica and failover
Nightly exports to Cloud Storage in the same region
Weekly backups copied to a multi-region Cloud Storage bucket
options.note: RPO of up to a week.

explanation: An RTO of minutes with RPO near zero needs a replicated, failover-capable design: Cloud SQL Enterprise Plus with a cross-region replica. Nightly or weekly backups, or a single zone, have far worse RPO/RTO.

refs.title: About high availability | Cloud SQL for MySQL

scenario: Which load balancer should front a global HTTPS application with backends in several regions?

options.text: Regional external passthrough Network Load Balancer

explanation: The global external Application Load Balancer fronts a global HTTPS app with backends in several regions, and Cloud CDN and Cloud Armor attach to it. Regional internal and passthrough balancers are regional.

scenario: A media company wants to cut egress costs and latency for static video segments worldwide. What should be added?

options.text: Cloud CDN (or Media CDN) in front of the origin
More web server VMs in the origin region
A multi-region Cloud Storage bucket without a CDN
options.note: Still served from storage locations, not edge caches.

explanation: Cloud CDN or Media CDN caches static content at the edge, cutting latency and egress from the origin. More origin VMs or Cloud NAT don't cache globally.

scenario: Which storage option suits petabytes of rarely accessed archival data that must be kept for compliance?

options.text: Cloud Storage Archive class with a retention policy
Persistent Disk snapshots stored in a multi-region location

explanation: Cloud Storage Archive class with a retention policy suits petabytes of rarely accessed data kept for compliance, and Bucket Lock makes the retention immutable. Filestore and Memorystore are for active data.

scenario: A company wants to migrate VMware VMs to Google Cloud quickly without refactoring. What fits?

options.text: Convert all apps to Cloud Run functions

explanation: Google Cloud VMware Engine runs VMware workloads in Google Cloud with no refactoring. Migrate to Virtual Machines can instead convert VMs to Compute Engine; rewriting for Cloud Run is a refactor.

scenario: Which tool helps discover on-premises assets, estimate TCO and plan migration waves?
explanation: Migration Center discovers on-premises assets, estimates TCO and rightsizing, and helps plan migration waves. Asset Inventory covers resources already in Google Cloud.

scenario: A team wants to build an enterprise AI agent grounded in company documents with minimal custom code. What should they use?

options.text: Agent Studio and Agent Search on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform
A custom LLM trained from scratch on GKE
BigQuery full-text search with scheduled queries
options.note: Search only; no agent or grounding.

explanation: Agent Studio and Agent Search (formerly Vertex AI Search) on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform provide grounded retrieval over company documents with minimal code. Training from scratch or SQL full-text search is far more work.

scenario: Which Google Cloud framework provides best practices across operational excellence, security, reliability, cost and performance?
explanation: The Google Cloud Well-Architected Framework gives best practices across operational excellence, security, reliability, cost and performance, plus sustainability and AI/ML perspectives. ITIL is an unrelated service-management framework.

scenario: Which architecture pattern decouples services so a slow consumer doesn't block producers?
explanation: Asynchronous messaging with Pub/Sub decouples services so a slow consumer doesn't block producers, improving resilience and scalability. Synchronous chained calls and shared databases couple them tightly.

scenario: A workload needs GPUs for training large models with high-speed interconnects. Which offering helps?

options.text: Spot VMs with a single GPU each
options.note: No high-speed interconnect for large training.

options.text: Cloud Run with GPUs for every training step
options.note: Suited to inference, not large distributed training.

explanation: AI Hypercomputer provides GPU or TPU clusters with high-speed interconnects for large-model training; TPUs are Google's custom AI accelerators. Cloud Run or single Spot GPUs don't give that scale.

scenario: Which design improves availability for a regional application at the lowest complexity?

options.text: Spread instances across multiple zones with a regional MIG
Place all VMs in one zone
Use a zonal MIG with autoscaling
options.note: Still exposed to a zone outage.

explanation: A regional managed instance group spreads VMs across zones, so a zone failure doesn't take the app down, with low added complexity. One large VM or a single zone is a single point of failure.

scenario: A company needs its data to stay in Germany. Which design choice is essential?

options.text: Deploy in a German region and enforce location with organization policy
Encrypt data with CMEK and store it in any region

explanation: Data residency in Germany needs deployment in a German region and an organization policy (resource locations) that enforces it. CMEK alone doesn't constrain location, and multi-region US buckets violate it.

scenario: Which API management platform helps expose backend services securely to partners with quotas and analytics?
explanation: Apigee is the API management platform for exposing backend services securely to partners, with quotas, analytics, monetization and developer portals. Cloud NAT and DNS aren't API managers.

scenario: Which choice reduces cost for a batch analytics workload that can tolerate interruptions?
explanation: Spot VMs with checkpointing cut cost for interruption-tolerant batch analytics, since jobs restart from checkpoints after preemption. Three-year commitments and sole-tenant nodes cost more.

scenario: A team needs a fully managed Kubernetes environment where Google manages nodes and security hardening. What fits?

options.text: GKE Standard with manual node pools

explanation: GKE Autopilot is fully managed Kubernetes where Google manages nodes and hardening and bills per pod resource requests. Self-managed Kubernetes and Standard node pools leave management to you.

scenario: Which storage service gives high-performance managed file shares for HPC workloads on Google Cloud?
explanation: Google Cloud Managed Lustre provides high-performance managed file shares for HPC. Filestore and NetApp Volumes serve general NFS/SMB workloads, and Cloud Storage isn't a POSIX file system.

scenario: Which approach makes an architecture cost-efficient for variable demand?

options.text: Use autoscaling and pay-per-use managed services
Provision for peak load all year
Use the largest machine types everywhere
Buy committed use discounts for peak capacity

explanation: Autoscaling and pay-per-use managed services match spend to variable demand. Provisioning for peak or committing for peak capacity wastes money; FinOps practices align cost with value.

scenario: Several teams need their own projects but a central network team must control subnets and firewall policy. What design fits?

options.text: Shared VPC with a host project and service projects
A separate auto mode VPC per project
VPC peering between every project pair

explanation: Shared VPC lets a central network team own subnets and firewall policy in a host project while teams deploy in service projects. Separate auto mode VPCs or pairwise peering fragment control.

scenario: A company needs a dedicated 10 Gbps private connection from its data center to Google Cloud. What should be used?

options.note: Over the internet, lower throughput per tunnel.
Too little bandwidth for this need.
Reaches Google public services, not your VPC.

explanation: Dedicated Interconnect gives a dedicated private connection (10 Gbps or 100 Gbps) from a data center to Google Cloud. Partner Interconnect suits lower bandwidth or no colocation, and HA VPN runs over the internet.

scenario: Which option privately connects consumers to a managed service in another VPC without peering?
explanation: Private Service Connect uses endpoints with internal IP addresses to privately reach managed services in another VPC, with no peering needed. Cloud NAT and public IPs expose or route differently.

refs.title: Private Service Connect | Virtual Private Cloud

scenario: VMs without external IPs need to access Google APIs privately. What's the simplest setting?

options.text: Enable Private Google Access on the subnet
Assign public IPs to every VM
Create a VPN to Google APIs
Route API traffic through Cloud NAT

explanation: Enabling Private Google Access on the subnet lets VMs without external IPs reach Google APIs privately; Private Service Connect endpoints are another option. Public IPs or a VPN aren't needed.

refs.title: Private Google Access | Virtual Private Cloud
Private Service Connect | Virtual Private Cloud

scenario: Which tool should be used to provision infrastructure consistently across environments?

options.text: Manual console clicks documented in a wiki

explanation: Terraform (directly or through Infrastructure Manager) provisions infrastructure consistently across environments from version-controlled code. Manual console steps and wiki notes aren't repeatable.

scenario: Which approach lets developers quickly create standard, approved environments themselves?

options.text: Application Design Center templates or IaC modules
Give everyone Owner on the organization
Email requests to the network team for every change
Share one project for all teams

explanation: Platform engineering provides golden paths such as Application Design Center templates or IaC modules, so developers self-serve standard approved environments. Granting Owner everywhere or emailing requests defeats governance.

scenario: A GKE cluster must keep pods from reaching each other unless explicitly allowed. What should be configured?

options.text: Firewall rules on the node pool's VMs
options.note: Coarse; doesn't control pod-to-pod traffic in the cluster.

explanation: Kubernetes network policies control which pods may talk to each other; GKE Dataplane V2 enforces them with eBPF. Separate node pools and node VM firewall rules don't govern pod-to-pod traffic.

refs.title: Control communication between Pods and Services using network policies | GKE

scenario: Which storage choice suits a stateful GKE workload needing a regional, replicated block volume?

options.text: Regional Persistent Disk (or Hyperdisk Balanced HA)
A Cloud Storage bucket as a block device

explanation: A regional Persistent Disk (or Hyperdisk Balanced HA) replicates synchronously across two zones, giving a stateful GKE workload a replicated block volume. Local SSD and emptyDir are ephemeral.

refs.title: Create and manage regional disks | Compute Engine

scenario: Which Compute Engine feature reduces boot disk management for many VMs by using a common image?

options.text: Custom images in an image family
Using community images from unknown publishers
Copying disks with dd per VM

explanation: Custom images in an image family give consistent boot disks across many VMs, and the family always points to the latest image. Installing each VM by hand or using unknown community images is error-prone.

refs.title: Image families best practices | Compute Engine

scenario: Which DNS design allows on-premises systems to resolve names of private Google Cloud resources?

options.text: Public Cloud DNS zones with private IPs
Editing hosts files on every server

explanation: A Cloud DNS inbound server policy (forwarding) lets on-premises systems resolve private Google Cloud names, while outbound forwarding zones resolve on-premises names from Google Cloud. Public zones shouldn't hold private IPs.

scenario: Which configuration supports high availability for HA VPN to on-premises?

options.text: Two tunnels from an HA VPN gateway with Cloud Router and BGP
Classic VPN with two gateways and static routes
options.note: Lower SLA; deprecated for new HA designs.

explanation: HA VPN with two tunnels, Cloud Router and BGP gives the 99.99% SLA. One tunnel with static routes or Classic VPN doesn't meet that availability.

scenario: A team wants serverless containers to reach resources in a VPC. What should be configured?

options.text: Direct VPC egress (or a Serverless VPC Access connector)
Private Google Access on the subnet

explanation: Direct VPC egress (or a Serverless VPC Access connector) lets serverless containers such as Cloud Run reach VPC resources; direct egress avoids managing connector instances. Private Google Access and Cloud NAT don't provide that path.

refs.title: Deploy container images to Cloud Run services

scenario: Which approach supports blue/green deployments for GKE workloads with minimal risk?

options.text: Deploy a new version alongside the old one and shift traffic via the load balancer or Gateway API
Update all pods in place at once
Delete the cluster and recreate it

explanation: Blue/green on GKE deploys the new version alongside the old and shifts traffic through the load balancer or Gateway API, and Cloud Deploy supports canary and blue/green strategies. In-place updates of everything at once are riskier.

scenario: Which service centrally manages releases to GKE and Cloud Run with promotion between environments?
explanation: Cloud Deploy manages releases to GKE and Cloud Run with promotion between environments, and approvals can gate production. Scheduler, Logging and DNS aren't delivery tools.

scenario: A company needs to connect many VPCs and on-premises sites with a hub-and-spoke model. What should be used?

options.note: One network, not hub-and-spoke between VPCs.

options.text: HA VPN tunnels between every pair of VPCs

explanation: Network Connectivity Center provides a hub-and-spoke model to connect many VPCs and on-premises sites, including SD-WAN integrations. Full-mesh peering or tunnels between every pair doesn't scale.

scenario: Which machine family is best for memory-intensive databases like SAP HANA?
explanation: Memory-optimized (M-series) machines suit memory-intensive databases like SAP HANA. E2 shared-core and compute-optimized families have too little memory per vCPU, and A3 is for accelerators.

refs.title: Machine families resource and comparison guide | Compute Engine

scenario: A healthcare company must prevent patient data in BigQuery from being copied to projects outside its perimeter. What should it use?

options.text: IAM deny policies on the dataset
options.note: Blocks principals, not data copied by authorized users.

explanation: VPC Service Controls creates a perimeter around BigQuery and other services to stop data being copied to projects outside it; combine with IAM and organization policies for defense in depth. Cloud Armor and firewall rules don't govern API data movement.

scenario: Applications on AWS must call Google Cloud APIs without long-lived keys. What should be designed?

options.text: Service account keys stored in AWS

explanation: Workload Identity Federation lets AWS workloads exchange their credentials for short-lived Google tokens, so there are no long-lived keys to store. Keys kept in AWS are still long-lived secrets.

scenario: Employees need secure access to internal web apps without a VPN. Which approach fits zero trust?

options.text: Identity-Aware Proxy with Chrome Enterprise Premium context-aware access
Open the apps to the internet with passwords
A flat network with no checks
IP allowlists on the load balancer

explanation: Identity-Aware Proxy with Chrome Enterprise Premium context-aware access grants access based on identity and device context, a zero-trust approach with no VPN. Open internet access or IP allowlists aren't identity-aware.

scenario: A financial firm must hold encryption keys outside Google Cloud. What option fits?

options.text: Customer-supplied encryption keys for every service
options.note: Limited service support, keys still provided to Google per request.

explanation: Cloud External Key Manager (EKM) keeps encryption keys outside Google Cloud, with a third-party key manager. Cloud HSM keeps hardware keys inside Google Cloud, and software KMS keys are in Google.

scenario: Which service discovers and de-identifies sensitive data like national IDs across storage and BigQuery?

options.note: Encrypts storage; data is still readable to users.

explanation: Sensitive Data Protection discovers and de-identifies sensitive data such as national IDs across storage and BigQuery, using masking, tokenization or format-preserving encryption. Cloud KMS only manages keys.

scenario: Which control prevents anyone from creating service account keys across the organization?

options.text: An IAM deny policy on each project
options.note: Possible but harder to manage than one org constraint.

explanation: The organization policy constraint iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation blocks service account key creation across the organization, and it's enforced by default on new organizations. A per-project IAM deny doesn't scale.

refs.title: Restrict IAM service account usage | Organization Policy

scenario: Which product protects generative AI apps from prompt injection and sensitive data leaks?

options.note: Finds sensitive data, but not prompt attacks.

explanation: Model Armor screens prompts and responses to protect generative AI apps from prompt injection and sensitive data leaks. Cloud Armor is a WAF for web apps and Sensitive Data Protection finds data.

scenario: Which service only allows signed, trusted container images to deploy to GKE or Cloud Run?
explanation: Binary Authorization allows only signed, trusted container images to deploy to GKE or Cloud Run, using attestations that images passed required checks. Cloud Deploy approvals gate releases, not image trust.

scenario: Which design gives administrators time-bound elevated access with approval?
explanation: Privileged Access Manager provides time-bound elevated access with approval (just-in-time), reducing standing privileges. Permanent Owner grants or shared admin accounts do the opposite.

scenario: Which service gives a central view of security posture, threats and vulnerabilities across the organization?
explanation: Security Command Center gives a central view of security posture, threats and vulnerabilities across the organization; Premium and Enterprise add threat detection and attack path simulation.

scenario: A company must prove regulatory compliance with controls for a specific region and framework. What helps?

options.note: Constraints, but not full compliance packages.

explanation: Assured Workloads helps meet regulatory frameworks by enforcing data residency and personnel access controls for a region and framework. Organization policy and VPC-SC alone don't cover personnel controls.

scenario: Which logs record Google personnel's access to customer content?
explanation: Access Transparency logs record Google personnel's access to customer content, and Access Approval lets customers approve it first. Admin Activity logs record customer-side admin actions.

scenario: Which principle should IAM design follow for workloads?

options.text: One service account per workload with least-privilege roles
One shared service account with Editor for everything

explanation: Use one service account per workload with only the roles it needs (least privilege), and use IAM Recommender to remove unused permissions. A shared Editor account or basic roles on the organization is too broad.

refs.title: Attach service accounts to resources | IAM

scenario: Which service protects public web apps against OWASP Top 10 attacks and DDoS at the edge?

options.note: VPC traffic, not web exploits at the edge.

explanation: Cloud Armor protects public web apps at the edge against OWASP Top 10 attacks and DDoS, and Adaptive Protection uses ML to detect Layer 7 attacks. Cloud NAT and NGFW aren't edge WAFs.

scenario: Which design stores database passwords and API keys securely for apps?

options.text: Cloud KMS keys used as passwords
options.note: KMS manages encryption keys, not app secrets.

explanation: Secret Manager with IAM-controlled access is the secure place for database passwords and API keys; rotate secrets and pin versions. Source control, metadata and environment variables leak easily.

scenario: Executives want to cut cloud costs without hurting performance. What's the best first step?

options.text: Review rightsizing and idle resource recommendations
Delete monitoring to save logging costs

explanation: Start cost reduction with Active Assist rightsizing and idle-resource recommendations (idle VMs, disks, IPs). Shutting down production or deleting monitoring harms the business.

scenario: A company's VM fleet runs at steady usage 24/7. Which pricing option reduces cost most predictably?

options.text: Spot VMs for the whole fleet

explanation: Committed use discounts reduce cost predictably for steady 24/7 usage, and flexible spend-based commitments apply across machine families. Spot VMs would risk interruption for the whole fleet.

scenario: Which practice aligns cloud spend with business value through shared responsibility for costs?
explanation: FinOps aligns cloud spend with business value through shared responsibility for costs, supported by labels, budgets and billing exports that show teams their costs.

refs.title: Export Cloud Billing data to BigQuery
Create and update labels for projects | Resource Manager

scenario: A business process requires a human to approve AI-generated insurance claim decisions. What design principle is this?
explanation: Requiring a person to approve AI-generated claim decisions is human-in-the-loop review. High-impact AI decisions benefit from human oversight; full automation removes that safeguard.

scenario: Which approach helps the team adopt cloud skills and change processes successfully?

options.text: Training, a cloud center of excellence and clear ownership
Centralize every decision with one person to keep control

explanation: Successful adoption pairs technology with training, a cloud center of excellence and clear ownership. Change management matters as much as tooling.

scenario: Which metric best measures whether a migration improved developer velocity?

options.text: Deployment frequency and lead time for changes (DORA)
Number of VMs migrated per week

explanation: DORA metrics such as deployment frequency and lead time for changes (plus change failure rate and time to restore) measure developer velocity. VM counts, invoices and IAM role counts don't.

scenario: A business needs to analyze customer behavior in near real time to personalize offers. Which architecture fits?

options.text: Pub/Sub to Dataflow to BigQuery with ML models
Nightly batch loads with BigQuery ML

explanation: Pub/Sub to Dataflow to BigQuery (with ML models) handles near real-time ingestion, processing and analysis for personalization. Weekly exports or nightly batches are too slow.

scenario: Which approach reduces risk when changing a critical business process to run on new cloud systems?

options.text: Pilot with a subset, measure, then roll out gradually
Switch everything at once on a Friday
Avoid informing stakeholders until it's done

explanation: Reduce migration risk by piloting with a subset, measuring, then rolling out gradually, with rollback plans and success criteria. A big-bang switch on a Friday without testing is the opposite.

scenario: Which analysis helps decide whether to rehost, replatform or refactor each application?
explanation: An application portfolio assessment weighs business value, complexity, dependencies and licensing to choose rehost, replatform or refactor for each app. Applying one approach to everything ignores those differences.

scenario: A company wants to estimate the costs of a new architecture before building it. What should be used?
explanation: The Google Cloud Pricing Calculator estimates the cost of a new architecture before you build it; Migration Center provides TCO estimates for migrations. Last month's invoice and budgets reflect existing spend.

scenario: Which SRE concept balances release velocity with reliability using allowed unreliability?
explanation: Error budgets balance release velocity with reliability by defining allowed unreliability; when it's spent, focus shifts to reliability work. Change freezes forever or unlimited releases ignore the balance.

scenario: Which licensing consideration matters when migrating Windows Server and SQL Server workloads?

options.text: Licenses never matter in the cloud
Licenses only matter for Linux distributions

explanation: Windows Server and SQL Server migrations need a licensing decision: bring your own license (sole-tenant nodes help with some BYOL rules) or use pay-as-you-go images. Licenses do matter in the cloud and don't transfer automatically.

scenario: A team wants to quickly prototype gen AI features without managing models. What's the best starting point?

options.text: Use Gemini models through Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform APIs
Build a GPU cluster and train a model from scratch
Hire annotators to label data first
Fine-tune an open model on GKE first

explanation: To prototype generative AI quickly, use Gemini models through the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform APIs, then evaluate quality, cost and safety. Training or fine-tuning a model first delays learning.

scenario: Developers want a consistent, Google-managed cloud development environment with access to private resources. What fits?
explanation: Cloud Workstations provides managed cloud development environments that run in containers inside your VPC with access to private resources. Personal laptops with shared keys are neither managed nor secure.

scenario: Which tool helps developers emulate Google Cloud services locally for testing, like Pub/Sub and Firestore?
explanation: Cloud SDK emulators (for example Pub/Sub and Firestore) let developers test locally without cloud costs. Pointing tests at production databases is risky.

scenario: Which CI service builds containers and runs tests on each commit?
explanation: Cloud Build builds containers and runs tests on each commit, and can push images to Artifact Registry. Cloud Deploy handles delivery rather than building.

scenario: Which API style should a team choose for high-performance service-to-service communication with strict contracts?
explanation: gRPC suits high-performance service-to-service communication with strict contracts; REST remains common for public APIs. FTP, SMTP and Telnet aren't API styles for this.

scenario: Which approach safely tests a new version with a small percentage of real users?
explanation: A canary deployment sends a small percentage of real users to the new version while you monitor error rates before increasing traffic. Big-bang releases expose everyone at once.

scenario: Which tool helps developers write and understand code with AI assistance in their IDE?

options.note: Helps with cloud operations, not IDE coding.

explanation: Gemini Code Assist helps developers write and understand code with AI in their IDE, and Gemini CLI offers assistance in the terminal. Gemini Cloud Assist is for operating cloud resources.

scenario: A migration must move 500 TB from on premises with limited bandwidth. What's best?
explanation: Transfer Appliance suits moving hundreds of terabytes when bandwidth is limited; Storage Transfer Service suits online transfers when bandwidth allows. A small VPN would take far too long.

scenario: Which technique keeps APIs backward compatible when releasing changes?

options.text: Versioning APIs and avoiding breaking changes
Renaming fields to match new conventions

explanation: Version APIs and avoid breaking changes to keep them backward compatible; Apigee and API Gateway help manage versions. Silent format changes or removing endpoints without notice break clients.

scenario: Which practice makes infrastructure changes reviewable and auditable?

options.text: Pull requests for IaC with automated plan checks
Shared admin passwords stored in a vault

explanation: Pull requests for IaC with automated plan checks make infrastructure changes reviewable and auditable; GitOps applies the same idea to Kubernetes. Console changes leave no review trail.

scenario: Which service manages database schema and data migrations from Oracle to PostgreSQL-compatible databases?
explanation: Database Migration Service migrates databases, including heterogeneous moves such as Oracle to PostgreSQL-compatible targets; Gemini can help convert code. Datastream replicates change data and Storage Transfer moves files.

scenario: Which testing type verifies the system handles expected peak traffic before launch?
explanation: Load testing verifies the system handles expected peak traffic before launch; chaos testing checks resilience to failures. Unit tests alone don't exercise capacity.

scenario: Which metrics define user-facing reliability targets for a service?
explanation: SLIs are measured against SLOs to define user-facing reliability targets. VM CPU or commit counts don't express user-facing reliability, and alerts should key on SLO burn rate rather than every metric.

scenario: Which alerting approach reduces noise while catching real user impact?
explanation: Alerting on SLO burn rate catches real user impact while cutting noise; multi-window burn-rate alerts balance speed and precision. Alerting on every warning log creates alert fatigue.

scenario: Which tool helps find which functions use the most CPU in production code?
explanation: Cloud Profiler runs continuously with low overhead to show which functions use the most CPU in production code. Trace shows request latency, and Logging shows events.

scenario: Which practice improves learning after incidents?
explanation: Blameless postmortems with tracked action items improve learning after incidents. Blaming individuals or deleting records discourages reporting and hides lessons.

scenario: Which tool provides a single place to manage alerts, dashboards and uptime checks?
explanation: Cloud Monitoring is the single place for alerts, dashboards and uptime checks, within Google Cloud Observability alongside Logging, Trace and Profiler. Cloud Build and Artifact Registry are delivery tools.

scenario: Which design helps GKE workloads survive a zone outage?

options.text: Regional clusters with pods spread across zones

explanation: Regional GKE clusters with pods spread across zones survive a zone outage; pod disruption budgets protect availability during maintenance. A single node or emptyDir state doesn't.

scenario: Which practice validates disaster recovery plans actually work?

options.text: Regular DR drills and restore tests
Writing a plan once and never testing it
Testing only in production during peak

explanation: Regular DR drills and restore tests prove the plan works and let you measure actual RTO and RPO. An untested plan or assumed backups is a common failure.

scenario: Which service provides personalized notifications about Google Cloud incidents affecting your projects?

options.note: Check your endpoints, not Google incidents.

explanation: Personalized Service Health sends notifications about Google Cloud incidents affecting your own projects and integrates with incident tools. The public status page shows general status.

scenario: Which approach automates responses to common operational issues?

options.text: Runbooks automated with Cloud Run functions or Workflows

explanation: Automating runbooks with Cloud Run functions or Workflows handles common operational issues and reduces toil, a key SRE goal. Manual fixes every time or disabling noisy alerts doesn't.

scenario: Which AI assistant helps operators investigate issues and summarize logs in the Google Cloud console?

options.note: Groups errors but doesn't investigate with AI.

explanation: Gemini Cloud Assist helps operators investigate issues and summarize logs in the console, with troubleshooting and optimization recommendations. Gemini Code Assist is for coding.

scenario: Which technique ensures a service degrades gracefully under overload?
explanation: Load shedding and rate limiting let a service degrade gracefully under overload; circuit breakers and retries with backoff also help. Accepting every request until it crashes does not.
